response: Israeli hospital preparedness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents can be improved by defining surge capacity based on a fixed number of casualties rather than a percentile of bed capacity. Research suggests that only 20% of arriving casualties will require immediate medical treatment. By implementing this concept, hospitals can better utilize national emergency health resources, both in preparation and in real-time, leading to more effective management of multiple casualty incidents. This approach may help improve the prediction of surge capacity and injury severity distribution, ultimately enhancing hospital preparedness for terrorism-related incidents.
